" Script Studio's vimrc, read when vim is turned on and again whenever it is saved. " Taken: the :map family (nnoremap, inoremap jk <Esc>, ...), let mapleader, " and :set of the options vim here knows. Nothing else runs. " A notecard dropped on the box in Script Studio Preferences, Editor, takes its place.

Disconnected: [COUNT] unsaved scripts and notecards are kept on this computer and offered at your next login.

Unsaved changes to this from an earlier session were kept, from [WHEN] -- before it was last saved.

Disconnected: nothing can be saved. What is here is kept on this computer and offered at your next login.

[FILE] is not on disk any more; saving writes it again.
You may no longer change this. What is here is kept; save a copy to keep it for good.

The kept changes put in, as one step to undo
The compiled part of this script is not what its source makes: it was changed outside the preprocessor, or what the script includes has changed. Saving replaces it.
Let the kept changes go; File > Recover Unsaved Changes still has them for a week

What is here, written to a file on this computer
Write the file again where it was
Load the script again, with what is here put back over it

Disconnected: [NAME] cannot be saved; it is kept for your next login.

[NAME]'s script is being loaded under what is here first; save again once it is in.
[NAME] is being saved; move it once the save is done.
Saving a copy of [NAME] to your inventory...
A copy of [NAME] is saved in your inventory; the tab it came from closed.
A copy of [NAME] is saved in your inventory; the tab it came from stays open, since it changed while the copy was made.
Return opens one with its changes; Shift-Return discards it
Nothing unsaved is kept from before, and nothing was discarded lately.
1 script kept from last time opened again, with its unsaved changes.
[COUNT] scripts kept from last time opened again, with their unsaved changes.

[NAME]'s kept changes let go of; File > Recover Unsaved Changes still has them for a week.
[NAME]'s kept changes let go of for good.
A new item in your inventory with what [NAME] holds, saved

What the script's code weighs for [TARGET]: [BYTES] of the [MAX] bytes it runs a script in. What it allocates as it runs is not in this.
About what the script's code weighs for [TARGET]: [BYTES] of the [MAX] bytes it runs a script in, estimated from the code its compiler makes. What it allocates as it runs is not in this.
Weighed before the preprocessor's optimizer, which a save runs: the saved script may weigh less.
Weighed as a save sends it, after the preprocessor.
The script's code comes to about [SIZE] KB, more than the [LIMIT] KB [TARGET] runs a script in.
The script's code is about [SIZE] KB, likely more than the [LIMIT] KB [TARGET] runs a script in.
The script's code is [SIZE] KB before the optimizer, more than the [LIMIT] KB [TARGET] runs a script in: it may fit once the optimizer has been over it.
What saving this script sends: [BYTES] of the [MAX] bytes a script may be. A preprocessed script is sent as written and as expanded, measured here before the optimizer and compression a save adds.
What saving this script sends: [BYTES] bytes, [OVER] more than the [MAX] a script may be. A save is refused until it is shorter.
The notecard's text: [BYTES] of the [MAX] bytes a notecard may hold.
The notecard's text: [BYTES] bytes, [OVER] more than the [MAX] a notecard may hold. A save is refused until it is shorter, since no viewer could open it past that.
[NAME] has no code of its own to weigh: a notecard, or a script that is only ever included.
[NAME] is weighed once it has been checked.
Weighed before the preprocessor's optimizer, which a save runs.
Weighed before the preprocessor's optimizer; as a save sends it, [SENT] KB.

What the script's code weighs as its compiler makes it, before it runs. What it allocates as it runs -- the lists it grows, the strings it builds -- is not in this, and is as often what stops a script.
[TARGET]: [BYTES] bytes of code, of the [MAX] it runs a script in.
[TARGET]: about [BYTES] bytes of code, of the [MAX] it runs a script in, estimated from the code its compiler makes.
[TARGET]: it does not compile for it: [ERROR]
The target the script is compiled for.
The state's table of handlers; the handlers are listed each on its own.
What the target spends on the script as a whole, whatever is in it.
[NAME]: [BYTES] bytes of code on [TARGET], [SHARE] of the [LIMIT] KB it runs a script in.
[NAME]: about [BYTES] bytes of code on [TARGET], [SHARE] of the [LIMIT] KB it runs a script in.
Line [LINE]: [BYTES] bytes of code on [TARGET], [SHARE] of the [LIMIT] KB it runs a script in.
Line [LINE]: about [BYTES] bytes of code on [TARGET], [SHARE] of the [LIMIT] KB it runs a script in.
What the script's code weighs on [TARGET] before the preprocessor's optimizer and after it, as this view shows it sent: [BYTESBEFORE] and then [BYTESAFTER] of the [MAX] bytes it runs a script in.

About what the script's code weighs on [TARGET] before the preprocessor's optimizer and after it, as this view shows it sent: [BYTESBEFORE] and then [BYTESAFTER] of the [MAX] bytes it runs a script in, estimated from the code its compiler makes.
[NAME] was sent, but by the studio's reckoning its code comes to about [SIZE] KB, more than the [LIMIT] KB [TARGET] runs a script in: the region may not compile it, or it may not run.
[NAME] was not saved: it is [SIZE] bytes, [OVER] more than the [LIMIT] a script may be.
Moving part of it into another script, or into a notecard it reads, would bring it under.
A preprocessed script is sent as written and as expanded: turning on Compress in the preprocessor's settings shrinks the expanded half.
A preprocessed script is sent as written and as expanded, and what it includes counts in the expanded half: including less, or moving part of it into another script, would bring it under.

menu_item_call.label: Reference for the Word at the Caret
menu_item_call.name: reference

button.name: save_btn
button.tool_tip: Save and compile the script ([KEYS]); a notecard is saved as it is

button.name: save_all_btn
button.tool_tip: Save every script with unsaved changes ([KEYS])

button.name: undo_btn
button.tool_tip: Undo the last change ([KEYS])

button.name: redo_btn
button.tool_tip: Redo what was undone ([KEYS])

button.name: find_btn
button.tool_tip: Find in this script ([KEYS]); [KEYS2] finds across scripts

button.name: format_btn
button.tool_tip: Put the script's indentation and spacing right ([KEYS])

button.name: expanded_btn
button.tool_tip: Show what the preprocessor made of this script, as the server compiles it, in place of the source; press again for the source ([KEYS]). Read-only. Off while the preprocessor is: Build > Preprocess on Save turns it on.

button.label: Explorer
button.name: fold_explorer
button.tool_tip: The objects in hand and their scripts, down the left ([KEYS])

button.label: Panel
button.name: fold_bottom
button.tool_tip: The panel under the editor: the problems ([KEYS]), the references ([KEYS2]), what the scripts say ([KEYS3]), and search ([KEYS4])

button.label: Inspector
button.name: fold_inspector
button.tool_tip: The outline and the symbol at the caret, down the right ([KEYS])

filter_editor.label: Filter
filter_editor.name: explorer_filter
filter_editor.tool_tip: Only the objects, prims, scripts and notecards with these letters in their names

panel.name: explorer_tree
panel.tool_tip: The objects in hand -- pinned, selected in world, or holding a script that is open -- and their scripts and notecards. Double-click or return opens one, delete deletes it, F2 renames it -- or an object or a prim -- where it stands, right-click for everything else. Drag them to your inventory or onto another object here, and drop on an object what your inventory holds, to put it in.

button.label: Open
button.name: explorer_open
button.tool_tip: Open the chosen scripts and notecards

button.label: Start
button.name: explorer_start
button.tool_tip: Set the chosen scripts running; every script of a chosen object or prim

button.label: Stop
button.name: explorer_stop
button.tool_tip: Stop the chosen scripts; every script of a chosen object or prim

button.label: Reset
button.name: explorer_reset
button.tool_tip: Reset the chosen scripts; every script of a chosen object or prim

button.name: explorer_refresh
button.tool_tip: Refresh: ask the region for what the objects hold again

tab_strip.name: tabs
tab_strip.tool_tip: The scripts open here, one tab each; the tab shown is the script being edited. From the keyboard, once Go to Tabs has put it here: the arrows choose, Shift with an arrow moves a tab, Delete closes one

button.name: notice_close
button.tool_tip: Hide this until there is something else to say

jump_bar.name: breadcrumb
jump_bar.tool_tip: Where the caret is: the line and column at the right, and from the script down to the symbol around it at the left. Press a step to go there; press its arrow to pick one of the symbols beside it instead.

combo_box.name: experience
combo_box.tool_tip: The experience the script runs under, which its experience functions need: none, one you contribute to, or the one it has. Picked here, it is set when the script is saved.

button.name: experience_profile
button.tool_tip: The profile of the experience the script runs under

button.label: Reset
button.name: reset_btn
button.tool_tip: Reset the script in its object: its state forgotten and state_entry run again

check_box.label: Running
check_box.name: running
check_box.tool_tip: Whether the script runs in its object; a save keeps whatever this says

combo_box.name: compile_target
combo_box.tool_tip: What the script compiles for when it is saved: an LSL script on Mono (the usual choice), on the legacy LSL2 machine, or on Luau; an SLua script as SLua. A script written in one language compiles for that language's targets only.

check_box.label: Errors
check_box.name: problems_errors
check_box.tool_tip: Show what stops the script from compiling or running

check_box.label: Warnings
check_box.name: problems_warnings
check_box.tool_tip: Show what probably does not do what was written

check_box.label: Notes
check_box.name: problems_notes
check_box.tool_tip: Show what is worth a look: the optimizer's changes, the lint's advice

check_box.label: Fixable
check_box.name: problems_fixable
check_box.tool_tip: Show only the problems that offer a fix, which the right-click menu, Control-. and the lightbulb make

combo_box.name: problems_scope
combo_box.tool_tip: Whose problems: the script in front, or every script open here, each under its name

combo_box.name: problems_origin
combo_box.tool_tip: Only what one source said: the checkers, the compiler, the preprocessor, the optimizer, the script as it ran

filter_editor.label: Filter
filter_editor.name: problems_filter
filter_editor.tool_tip: Only problems with these words in them

pane_list.name: problems
pane_list.tool_tip: What the compiler and the analyzers said. Choosing one shows it in the script, and the arrow keys walk the list; return or a double-click goes there to type, escape goes back.

pane_list.name: references
pane_list.tool_tip: Every place the name last looked up stands, in the script it was looked up from and in the object's others, whichever tab is in front. Choosing one shows it, and the arrow keys walk the list; return or a double-click goes there to type.

combo_box.name: output_filter
combo_box.tool_tip: Whose words to show: every object's, the scripts open here, your own objects', or one object's

combo_box.name: output_kind
combo_box.tool_tip: What kind of thing to show: the run-time errors alone, what scripts told their owner, the debug channel, or what the studio itself did -- saving, compiling, preprocessing

filter_editor.label: Filter
filter_editor.name: output_find
filter_editor.tool_tip: Only what says these words, or comes from a name with them in it

button.label: Clear
button.name: output_clear
button.tool_tip: Forget what was said so far; the filters stay as they are

button.label: Copy All
button.name: output_copy
button.tool_tip: What the pane shows through its filters, on the clipboard as it reads

output_view.name: output
output_view.placeholder: What the scripts say on the debug channel and to their owner appears here, as it is said. A script's name is a link to it, at the line of a run-time error.

scope_bar.name: search_bar
scope_bar.tool_tip: A search said as a sentence: the words, how they have to match, and where to look. Return runs it, and changing a word runs it again.

button.label: Replace All
button.name: search_replace
button.tool_tip: Every place found replaced by the words in the box, script by script, each script's own one step to undo, once you say so. A script that is not open is opened with the change unsaved.

line_editor.label: Replace with
line_editor.name: search_replacement
line_editor.tool_tip: What to put in place of the words found; return or Replace All asks before replacing

pane_list.name: search_results
pane_list.tool_tip: Every place the words were found, kept up to date as the scripts open here are typed in. Choosing one shows it, and the arrow keys walk the list; return or a double-click goes there to type.

pane_list.name: weights_targets
pane_list.tool_tip: What the script's code would weigh on each target it could be compiled for, beside what each runs a script in: which is how to choose one. Choosing one lists its parts.

pane_list.name: weights_parts
pane_list.tool_tip: What each part of the script weighs on the target chosen: its bytes, its share of what the target runs a script in, and how that moved since the script was last saved. Choosing one shows it, and the arrow keys walk the list; return or a double-click goes there to type.

combo_box.name: outline_sort
combo_box.tool_tip: How the symbols are ordered under what holds them: as the script has them, by name, or by kind

filter_editor.label: Filter
filter_editor.name: outline_filter
filter_editor.tool_tip: Only the symbols with these letters in their names

pane_list.name: outline
pane_list.tool_tip: What the script declares, the one the caret is in chosen; the arrow before a symbol folds what it holds. Choosing one shows it, and the arrow keys walk the list, left and right folding; return or a double-click goes there to type.

text_view.name: symbol
text_view.placeholder: The symbol at the caret: its declaration, its documentation and its page on the wiki. F1 looks up the word at the caret; Help browses the whole reference.
